title: Murder in the Bath

panels.visual: Ten years earlier, at Aulis: King Agamemnon (bronze breastplate, dark beard) at an altar by the sea with his daughter Iphigenia in white, priests, becalmed ships
panels.caption: Ten years before, King Agamemnon had sacrificed his own daughter, Iphigenia, to get a wind to sail to Troy.

panels.visual: Queen Clytemnestra (dark hair, gold diadem) weeping alone in the palace, then her face hardening
panels.caption: Her mother, Queen Clytemnestra, never forgave him.

panels.visual: Agamemnon returning to Mycenae through the Lion Gate in a chariot piled with treasure, crowds cheering
panels.caption: Ten years later Agamemnon came home from Troy, victorious and rich.

panels.visual: Clytemnestra smiling sweetly, rolling out a long red carpet up the palace steps
panels.caption: She laid a red carpet for him and smiled.

speech.speaker: Clytemnestra
speech.text: Welcome home, husband. Your bath is ready.

panels.visual: Agamemnon relaxing in a steaming bath in a dark palace room
panels.caption: He went to wash off the long journey.

panels.visual: Clytemnestra throwing a heavy net over Agamemnon as he steps out of the bath, so he cannot move
panels.caption: As he stepped out, she threw a net over him so he could not move.

panels.visual: The shadow of Clytemnestra raising an axe on the wall, dark-red splashes
panels.caption: Then she killed him with an axe.

panels.visual: At night, a young girl (his sister Electra) smuggling the little boy Orestes out of the palace
panels.caption: Their little son Orestes was smuggled away to safety.

panels.visual: Years later: Orestes, now a young man with a sword, returning to the palace; Clytemnestra's shadow, red drips
panels.caption: Years later Orestes came home and killed his mother, to avenge his father.

panels.visual: The Furies, snake-haired spirits of revenge with bat wings and long black robes, chasing Orestes across mountains
panels.caption: Then the Furies hunted him across the world.

panels.visual: Orestes on trial on the rocky Areopagus in Athens; the goddess Athena dropping a white pebble
panels.caption: He fled to Athens. On the Areopagus, Athena cast the deciding vote and set him free.

panels.visual: Today: the polished grey rock of the Areopagus below the Acropolis, two girls and Glauka climbing it
panels.caption: That rock is real: the Areopagus, just below the Acropolis. You can climb it.

mood: Gothic horror mood for this story: dark palace shadows, torchlight, one dark-red accent colour; blood shown as splashes and drips, never wounds; frightening but suitable for brave children aged 9 to 11.
